annotation.authors_or_issuer: López Cañellas, N.; Kerr, A.; Vaughan, B.
annotation.summary_en: Short conference paper presenting a thematic review of 40 Web of Science articles on AI ethics and policy in workplace human-robot collaboration. It finds EU value-sensitive design dominant but criticised as insufficient, and argues regulation needs interdisciplinary approaches, scrutiny of underlying narratives, and worker and union involvement.
key_provisions_or_claims: Thematic review of 40 peer-reviewed articles selected from 2753 Web of Science entries.
EU policy combines consequentialist risk tiers (AI Act) and virtue-based ethics guidelines.
Value-sensitive design is dominant but criticised as insufficient to prevent harms.
Calls for interdisciplinary policymaking and stakeholder exchange, which remain scarce in practice.
Recommends shifting from automation to augmentation, with trade unions involved in design and decisions.
annotation.title_clean: Building Resilient Governance Frameworks for Human-Robot Collaboration: Towards a More Interdisciplinary Understanding of Risk and Ethics in European Regulation
annotation.title_en: Building Resilient Governance Frameworks for Human-Robot Collaboration: Towards a More Interdisciplinary Understanding of Risk and Ethics in European Regulation
annotation.venue: Proceedings of the 33rd European Safety and Reliability Conference (ESREL 2023)
